metadata.title: The Dollmaker's Workshop
metadata.description: You wake on the cold stone floor of a basement workshop. Porcelain faces stare from every shelf. Upstairs, an elderly woman hums a lullaby — and she's making a mold. Of you.
metadata.author: captive-examples

setting.ambient_text: The smell of lacquer and old fabric. Porcelain eyes glint in dim light. Above you, floorboards creak and a woman hums.

items.name: Glass Eyes
items.description: A handful of blue glass eyes. Cold and disturbingly realistic.

then.text: Each iris is hand-painted with tiny veins. They feel heavier than they should.

items.name: Bent Wire
items.description: A stiff wire from a doll armature. Could pick a simple lock.

then.text: Copper wire, about six inches. One end is bent into a small hook.

items.name: Torn Journal Page
items.description: A page ripped from Madame Voss's journal.

then.text: 'Process batch 14. Cabinet combination: 3-8-1. The new subject arrives Thursday.' The handwriting is precise, almost mechanical.
'Process batch 14. Cabinet combination: 3-8-1.' In the margin, glowing under UV: 'They never stop screaming. I just learned to stop hearing.' And a date: 'Oct 3, 1987'.

items.name: Small Mirror
items.description: A handheld vanity mirror. The glass is cracked but usable.

then.text: You flip it over. Scratched into the metal backing: the number '42'. Whose hand etched this?
A cracked vanity mirror. '42' scratched on the back.

items.name: UV Flashlight
items.description: A small ultraviolet flashlight. Makes certain substances glow.

then.text: Industrial grade. Used for checking paint curing. The battery indicator shows half charge.

items.name: Hydrochloric Acid
items.description: A brown glass bottle. The label reads 'HCl — DANGER'.

then.text: Concentrated hydrochloric acid. Used for etching porcelain. Would dissolve metal given enough time.

items.name: Lacquer Thinner
items.description: A tin of industrial lacquer thinner. Flammable.

then.text: Methyl ethyl ketone. Extremely flammable. Fumes can cause unconsciousness in enclosed spaces.

items.name: Cloth Rag
items.description: A stained rag that smells of turpentine.

then.text: Heavy cotton. Stained with paint and something darker.

items.name: Soaked Rag
items.description: A rag saturated with lacquer thinner fumes. Potent.

then.text: The fumes are overpowering. Don't breathe too deeply. Could incapacitate someone briefly.

items.name: Ornate Key
items.description: A small brass key with a decorative bow shaped like a rose.

then.text: Delicate and ornate. Too small for a door lock. The bow is shaped like a rose — a winding key?

items.name: Rolled Paper
items.description: A tiny scroll of paper pulled from inside a doll's head.

then.text: A hand-drawn diagram of the workshop's pipe system. An arrow points to a valve in the main room labeled 'RELEASE'. Below it: 'The water loosens everything.'

items.name: Rope Coil
items.description: A coil of sturdy hemp rope. About 20 feet.

then.text: Strong hemp rope. Enough to climb down from a height, or to lower through a grate to someone below.

items.name: Lockpick Set
items.description: A leather case with three thin metal picks.

then.text: Professional grade. The ally in the sub-basement must have had these. One pick is bent but two are still good.

items.name: Coal Chunk
items.description: A fist-sized lump of coal from the bin.

then.text: Dense and heavy. Could fuel the furnace — or be thrown as a distraction.

items.name: Music Box Cylinder
items.description: A tiny brass cylinder with pins. It plays a melody.

then.text: The pin pattern matches the lullaby Voss hums. Engraved on the base: 'For my little ones — M.V.'

items.name: Working Fuse
items.description: A ceramic screw-in fuse. The only one that isn't blown.

then.text: 15 amp ceramic fuse. Every other fuse in the box is blown. This is the only working one.

items.name: Paint Bucket
items.description: A half-full bucket of thick white primer.

then.text: Heavy. The primer is thick as paste. Would make a terrible mess if it fell on someone.

combinations.message: You soak the rag with lacquer thinner. The fumes are immediate and potent. Keep this away from your own face.

objects.name: Binding Ropes
objects.description: Rough hemp rope tied around your wrists and ankles.

then.text: You strain against the ropes, twisting your wrists. The hemp is old — it frays. With one final wrench, your hands pull free.
Rough hemp rope. Old and fraying at the edges. You could work your way free with enough effort.
A pile of frayed rope on the floor. You're free.

objects.name: Jar of Glass Eyes
objects.description: A large mason jar filled with glass eyes in various colors.

then.text: Dozens of glass eyes float in clear preservative. Blue, brown, green — all staring at nothing. They're disturbingly well-crafted.
You reach in and grab a handful of glass eyes. They click together in your palm like marbles.

objects.name: Workbench
objects.description: A long wooden workbench covered in tools and doll parts.

then.text: A wide workbench cluttered with sculpting tools, paint pots, and porcelain pieces. A magnifying lamp hangs over it. There's more to see up close.

objects.name: Chemical Cabinet
objects.description: A glass-fronted cabinet with various bottles and solutions.

then.text: A glass-fronted cabinet. Through the glass you can see bottles of chemicals, a small UV flashlight, and what looks like acid. A combination dial lock secures the door.
The cabinet stands open. Some bottles remain — solvents, fixatives, things you don't want to touch.
You smash the glass with your elbow. Shards scatter across the floor. The crash echoes through the basement.
You smash the glass. The sewing machine's clatter swallows most of the sound.
You work the wire into the simple lock. Click. The cabinet door swings open silently.
You push the cabinet door closed and rearrange the remaining bottles to fill the gaps. At a glance, nothing looks disturbed.
Reaching behind the chemical bottles, your fingers close around something metallic. A set of lock picks, hidden behind the back row — perhaps left by a previous captive.

objects.name: Cabinet Chemicals
objects.description: Bottles and tools inside the chemical cabinet.

then.text: You take the UV flashlight. It hums faintly when you click it on.
You carefully lift the acid bottle. The liquid sloshes ominously.
You take the tin of lacquer thinner. Flammable warnings cover every surface.

objects.name: Cellar Door
objects.description: A heavy wooden door with a thick chain and padlock.

then.text: A thick oak door. A heavy chain loops through the handle and a padlock holds it fast. Above the handle, someone painted the word 'PUSH' in red.
The chain hangs loose. The word 'PUSH' is painted above the handle. But wait — the hinges are on this side. That means it opens inward. It pulls, not pushes.
You pull at the chain. It's solid steel — not breaking this by hand.
You pour the acid over the chain links. It hisses and smokes. After a minute, the weakened link snaps. The chain falls away.
You work the picks into the padlock. It's a heavy-duty lock but the mechanism is old. Click. The padlock drops and the chain slides free.
You push the door. It doesn't budge. It must be barred from the other side too. There has to be another way.
The hinges are on YOUR side. Ignore 'PUSH' — you PULL. The heavy door groans open. Stone steps lead up into darkness. Freedom! But wait—
The ornate key is far too small for this padlock. It's meant for something delicate — a jewelry box? A music box?

objects.name: Inner Door
objects.description: A second door at the top of the short stairway.

then.text: A newer door. A digital keypad lock glows red beside the handle. Four digits.

then.reason: You push through the door and stumble up into the moonlit yard. The cold night air fills your lungs. You run and you don't stop. You're free.

objects.name: Coal Furnace
objects.description: A squat cast-iron furnace with a thick chimney pipe.

then.text: A heavy cast-iron furnace. Cold now, but there are embers in the grate. A control panel is mounted on the side. Worth a closer look.

objects.name: Boarded Window
objects.description: A small window boarded up from the inside.

then.text: A narrow basement window. One plank is nailed across it. Moonlight seeps around the edges.
Two planks now. Voss added another board after her last visit. Less moonlight gets through.
Three thick planks. The window is almost completely sealed. Getting through this would take serious effort now.
You pry at the board. The nails are stubborn but the wood is soft. It comes free with a crack.
Two boards now. You wrench them free one at a time, nails screaming against wood.
Three boards. This takes real effort. You wrench and pull, sweat stinging your eyes, wood splintering.
The window is too small to climb through. But the cold air feels like hope.
You douse the boards with thinner. The wood drinks it up. One match and these boards would be gone — but then, so might you. The furnace could provide a flame.

objects.name: Dumbwaiter
objects.description: A narrow shaft with a rope-and-pulley mechanism.

then.text: A dumbwaiter — a small platform on ropes, used to send things between floors. The shaft goes straight up. Worth investigating.

objects.name: Doll Shelves
objects.description: Floor-to-ceiling shelves lined with finished dolls.

then.text: Rows of porcelain dolls, each one unique. Their faces are... too real. Each one looks like a different person. You need a closer look.

objects.name: Sewing Machine
objects.description: An industrial sewing machine on a heavy metal table.

then.text: An industrial Singer. Threaded and ready. A foot pedal underneath. Loud when running — could cover other sounds.
You jam the foot pedal down with a scrap of wood. The machine roars to life, needle hammering up and down. Loud, but it'll cover your noise.
You kick the pedal loose. The machine winds down to silence.

objects.name: Pipe Valve
objects.description: A rusted water valve on an exposed pipe along the wall.

then.text: A water shutoff valve. The pipe runs down through the floor toward the furnace area.
You wrench the valve open. Water gurgles through the pipes in the wall. You hear it flowing down toward the furnace area.

objects.name: Shiny Key on Shelf
objects.description: A brass key sitting prominently on a high shelf, attached to a thin wire.

then.text: A shiny brass key on a high shelf. Conspicuously placed. A thin wire runs from it to... something behind the shelf. This might be a trap.
With the wire cut, you take the key safely. It's ornate — a rose pattern on the bow. Too small for a door.
You grab the key. The wire goes taut — CLANG! A small bell behind the shelf rings sharply. A trap!
You trace the wire to a small bell mechanism and carefully unhook it. The trap is disarmed.

objects.name: Stacked Crates
objects.description: Wooden shipping crates stacked against the wall.

then.text: Wooden crates stamped 'FRAGILE — PORCELAIN'. The gap behind them is just big enough to squeeze into.
You squeeze behind the crates, pulling loose fabric over yourself. In the darkness, you barely breathe.

objects.name: Bolt Hole
objects.description: A narrow space beneath the lowest shelf.

then.text: A narrow space beneath the heavy shelf. Dark. Just big enough if you curl up tight.
You slide beneath the shelf, pressing against the cold stone floor. Dust fills your nostrils. Don't sneeze.

objects.name: Basement Wall
objects.description: A stretch of bare stone wall with faint stains.

then.text: Bare stone. Water stains run down from above. Some scratches, but nothing legible.
Under the UV light, the wall comes alive. Someone wrote numbers in biological fluid — desperate last messages: '19' and 'HELP US'. Nineteen. Another number.

objects.name: Stairway
objects.description: The narrow stairs leading down from above. Where Voss enters.

then.text: Narrow wooden stairs going up. This is where she comes down. You can hear the floorboards creak above.
You press your ear to the stairwell. Humming. A lullaby. She's up there, working. The melody has a pattern — three notes high, two low, three high...
You scatter the glass eyes across the bottom steps. They roll into every crack and crevice. Anyone coming down will slip.
You balance the paint bucket on the edge of the top step, propped against the wall. When the door opens, it'll fall.

objects.name: Voss's Journal
objects.description: A leather-bound journal filled with meticulous handwriting.

then.text: Madame Voss's journal. Dated entries going back decades. One page is loose.
You flip through. Names. Dates. Measurements — of people. 'Subject 41: Female, 5'4", auburn hair. Completed Oct 1987.' 'Subject 42: Male, 5'11", dark hair. In progress.' That's you.
You tear out the loose page. It has the chemical cabinet combination on it.
Under UV, hidden notes appear between the lines. 'They never stop screaming. I just learned to stop hearing.' And dates circled in invisible ink — Oct 3, 1987 appears again and again.

objects.name: Small Mirror
objects.description: A handheld mirror lying among the tools.

then.text: A small vanity mirror, cracked but functional. Something is scratched on the metal backing.
You pocket the mirror. It's dual-purpose — a mirror for seeing around corners, and whatever that number on the back means.

objects.name: Armature Wire
objects.description: A piece of stiff copper wire used for doll armatures.

then.text: You bend the wire into a rough lockpick shape. Not elegant, but functional.

objects.name: Cloth Rag
objects.description: A stained work cloth draped over the edge.

then.text: You grab the rag. Heavy cotton, stained with paint.

objects.name: Paint Bucket
objects.description: A half-full bucket of white primer under the bench.

then.text: You carefully lift the paint bucket. Heavy. This could make a real mess.

objects.name: Fuse Box
objects.description: An old fuse box on the wall with three sockets.

then.text: Three fuse sockets labeled 'MAGNIFYING LAMP', 'UV STATION', 'DESK LAMP'. Only one working fuse — you'll have to choose which device gets power.
You screw the fuse into the magnifying lamp socket. The lamp hums to life, casting bright white light over the workbench.
You unscrew the fuse from the lamp socket and move it to UV STATION. The lamp dies; a faint purple glow fills the corner.
You move the fuse to DESK LAMP. The UV station goes dark; warm yellow light fills the workbench area.
You move the fuse back to MAGNIFYING LAMP. The desk lamp dies; the magnifier's bright ring lights up.
You pull a working fuse from the box. One of the spare slots had an extra.

objects.name: Furnace Controls
objects.description: A panel of dials and levers on the side of the furnace.

then.text: Three controls: a TEMPERATURE dial (Low/Medium/High/Max), an AIRFLOW lever (Closed/Half/Full), and a FUEL VALVE (Off/On/Boost). There are embers in the grate — it could be restarted.

objects.name: Coal Bin
objects.description: A metal bin half-full of coal chunks.

then.text: You grab a fist-sized lump of coal.

objects.name: Floor Grate
objects.description: A heavy iron grate in the floor near the furnace.

then.text: A heavy iron grate bolted into the stone floor. Through the gaps, darkness — and faint tapping from below.
You whisper into the grate. "Hello? Is someone down there?" A pause. Then a weak voice: "...who's there? Another one of her... projects?" The tapping stops.
"I've been here... weeks? Months? She takes pieces. Molds of my hands. My face. I can't feel my fingers anymore." The voice cracks. "Please. I need water. Something. Anything."
"Listen — the cellar door. She painted PUSH on it but the hinges are on your side. It PULLS open. And there's a second door with a keypad behind it."

You push the damp rag through the grate. Hands reach up to take it. "Thank you... thank you. I'll tell you everything I know. She has lockpicks in a case. I dropped them through the grate weeks ago — they should still be down here."

You lower the rope through the loosened grate. Frantic pulling. "I'm climbing! I'm — I see a ladder on the other side. I can reach the outside from here. Thank you. THANK YOU." Scrambling sounds fade. They're free. But the rope — they took the rope with them.
The grate is loose enough to lift. Below, you can see the sub-basement — and a rusty ladder on the far wall leading to a hatch. But it's a 12-foot drop. You'd need the rope to get down safely.
Water seeps around the grate bolts, loosening decades of rust. You pull — the grate shifts. One more pull and it lifts free.

objects.name: The Different Doll
objects.description: One doll stands out from the rest. Newer. More lifelike.

then.text: This doll is different. The face is eerily realistic — like a photograph rendered in porcelain. The eyes seem slightly loose in their sockets. A small '41' is painted on the base.
Under UV light, numbers glow on several dolls' bases. This one reads '41'. Each doll has a unique number. They're all... subjects.
You lift the doll from the shelf. The head wobbles. The glass eyes are loose — they rattle when you tilt it.
You work the loose glass eyes out of the sockets. Behind them — a tiny rolled paper stuffed into the hollow head.
You push replacement glass eyes into the doll's sockets and set it back on the shelf. It looks undisturbed.

objects.name: Music Box
objects.description: An ornate wooden music box among the dolls.

then.text: A beautiful music box with a rose inlay on the lid. There's a keyhole shaped like a rose. The same lullaby melody Voss hums is engraved on a brass plate.

The rose key turns perfectly. The lid opens and the lullaby plays — tinkling and delicate. Inside: a brass cylinder with the melody's pin pattern, and coiled beneath it, a length of rope. She hid it here. Why?

objects.name: Dumbwaiter Platform
objects.description: A small wooden platform on fraying ropes.

then.text: The platform can carry about 50 pounds. The ropes run through pulleys to the kitchen above. If you could fit in... but you'd need to be sure the ropes hold.
You reinforce the fraying ropes with your own rope, knotting them securely. The platform feels solid now. You could ride this up.

then.reason: You squeeze onto the platform and pull yourself up, hand over hand. The ropes creak but hold. You emerge in a dark kitchen. The front door is unlocked. You slip out into the night, leaving the house of dolls behind forever.

objects.name: Scratched Wall
objects.description: Deep scratches in the wooden shaft wall.

then.text: Deep gouges in the wood. Someone clawed at this wall. Random scratches — unless you're looking from the right angle.

You angle the mirror to see the scratches from above. They're not random — they form a rough map of the basement. An 'X' marks the pipe valve in the main room, with an arrow pointing down to the grate.

on_solve.text: Click. Click. Click. The lock releases and the cabinet door swings open.

on_fail.text: The dial clicks but nothing happens. Wrong combination.

on_solve.text: The keypad flashes green. The lock clicks open. Beyond: stone steps and cold air.

on_fail.text: The keypad flashes red. Wrong code.

config.wrong_step_message: The furnace sputters. Wrong order — it resets.

on_solve.text: The furnace roars to life. The iron glows red. The chimney shakes. The rumbling is LOUD — audible throughout the entire house.

config.wrong_step_message: A discordant clang. The box resets.

on_solve.text: The lullaby plays perfectly. A hidden compartment in the music box slides open, revealing a folded note with the number '19' circled.

phases.name: Trapped

on_enter.text: Cold stone against your cheek. The smell of lacquer and old fabric. Your wrists burn — rough rope. As your eyes adjust, porcelain faces emerge from the gloom. Dozens of them. Staring.

phases.ambient_text: A lullaby drifts from above. Gentle. Patient. Wrong.

phases.name: Free

on_enter.text: You stand on shaking legs. The workshop stretches around you — workbenches, shelves of dolls, a furnace, a heavy door. Above, the humming continues. She doesn't know you're loose. Yet.

phases.ambient_text: The lullaby continues above. Each note a countdown.

on_enter.text: The humming stops. A long silence. Then, quietly: "Oh, my little one... you've been naughty." Footsteps cross the floor above. Slow. Deliberate.

effects.text: The furnace roars. Upstairs, frantic footsteps — Voss rushes toward the source of the noise.
The furnace rumble dies down. You hear Voss muttering about the 'wretched boiler' as she returns upstairs.
Above you, the humming stops. A door opens. Footsteps on the stairs. "Time to check on my newest creation..." Voss is coming for her first visit.
The bell's echo reaches upstairs. The humming stops cold. "What was that?"
The lacquer thinner fumes hit the furnace heat. Thick white smoke billows through the workshop. Voss won't be able to see when she comes down.
The lullaby above changes tempo. Faster. More urgent. She's almost done preparing the mold. Time is running out.

killer.name: Madame Voss
killer.description: An elderly dollmaker. Soft-spoken. Patient. She hums lullabies while she works and calls her victims 'little ones'. Her cruelty is gentle, methodical, and absolute.

on_approach: Time to check on my little one...
Are you being good down there?
Almost ready for your fitting, dear.
on_search: Come now, darling. Don't hide from Madame.
I can hear you breathing, little one...
The others tried to hide too. They're on the shelf now.
on_clear: Sleep well, little one. Tomorrow we begin.
on_evidence: Oh my. Someone's been busy. Naughty, naughty.
You've been touching my things. That won't do.
Tsk tsk. Now I'll have to take precautions.
on_catch: There you are, my darling. The mold is ready. Hold very, very still.

effects.text: Voss sees the open cabinet. Her eyes narrow. "You've been in my chemicals." Her voice is ice.
Voss notices the disturbed doll. "Who's been touching my children?" She straightens it carefully, then looks around with cold suspicion.
You hear hammering. Voss is adding another board to the window.
More hammering. A third board across the window. She's sealing you in.
A crash and a shriek from the stairway. "MY EYES! My beautiful eyes — all over the —" Stumbling. Cursing. Voss retreats upstairs, limping. That bought you time.
SPLAT. The paint bucket crashes down. White primer coats Voss from head to shoulders. She screams — a sound you'd never expect from that gentle voice. She retreats upstairs to clean up.

special_behaviors.description: Voss rushes to check the furnace rumbling.
Voss slips on glass eyes and retreats.

win_conditions.description: Escape through the cellar door (chain + pull + keypad)
Ride the reinforced dumbwaiter to the kitchen
Free the sub-basement captive (they escape; you must find another way)

lose_conditions.description: Caught by Voss while not hiding

lose_conditions.message: The lullaby ends. Footsteps descend. "The mold is ready, little one. Time for your fitting." The door opens. Madame Voss stands there with plaster-coated hands and a smile that never reaches her eyes. It's too late.
lose_conditions.description: Ran out of time — Voss completes the mold

hints.text: Those ropes look old. Try pulling free.
The glass eyes could be taken. They might be useful beyond this jar.
The journal on the workbench might have useful information.
The chemical cabinet has a combination lock. The code might be in the journal.
Try the UV flashlight on different surfaces — walls, dolls, the journal.
The voice through the furnace grate knows things about this place. Build trust.
The keypad needs four digits. The doll numbers, the UV wall, and the mirror back all have numbers...
Listen at the stairway to hear the lullaby pattern. It matches the music box.

solution_paths.name: The Door Path
solution_paths.description: Escape through the cellar door using acid or lockpicks, discover the pull trick, and solve the keypad.

steps.note: Quiet path via wire — Noise Tradeoff

steps.action: look doll_shelves → closeup → use uv_flashlight on special_doll (find doll 41)
go furnace_closeup → talk furnace_grate (build ally trust)
use cloth_rag on furnace_grate (gain ally trust high)
talk furnace_grate (learn door pulls, not pushes)

steps.note: Point of No Return — acid consumed

steps.action: hand cellar_door (PULL — door opens! False Summit: second door found)
Cross-reference: doll 42, UV wall 19, mirror 42, journal Oct 3 1987 → code 4219

solution_paths.name: The Dumbwaiter Path
solution_paths.description: Escape via the dumbwaiter shaft after finding the rope in the music box and reinforcing the platform.

steps.action: use bent_wire on shelf_key (disarm bell trap)
look doll_shelves → use doll_key on music_box (get rope + cylinder)
steps.note: Red Herring resolved — key fits music box, not cellar door

steps.action: look dumbwaiter_shaft → use small_mirror on dumbwaiter_scratches (Perspective Alignment)

solution_paths.name: The Savior Path
solution_paths.description: Free the sub-basement captive via the loosened grate, then escape via dumbwaiter or door.

steps.action: hand pipe_valve (open — Echo pattern: water flows to furnace area)
go furnace_closeup → hand furnace_grate (water loosened it)
talk furnace_grate → build trust → use rope on grate (free ally)
Must now use cellar door path (no rope for dumbwaiter)
